chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man to whom a domestic pigeon was gifted and brought while he was in the sanctuary (Haram) in a state of Ihram. He said: 'If he eats from it, he should give in charity the equivalent of its price.' And domestic birds, when brought into the sanctuary, should not be touched either; rather, their way is left open. And if it has a clipped wing, it is left until its feathers grow back, then it is released.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim in Ihram who catches a bird in the Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies the kaffarah for accidentally catching a domestic bird within the Haram boundaries, mandating that the pilgrim pay its value in charity rather than offering the bird itself. It further details the humane handling of the captured bird, instructing that it be released unharmed, with specific provisions for those with clipped wings to ensure their recovery before release. This ruling highlights the precision of Shia fiqh in distinguishing between accidental transgression and the method of compensation, emphasizing mercy towards the creature even during the sacred state of Ihram.
